initial_answer.text:
按NERC《无功规划》指南，动态无功资源随电网电压变化在指定电压带宽内连续、实时自动调节出力，可维持设定电压或按电压下垂特性运行；采用电力电子装置的设备调节可在电气周波级完成（如STATCOM响应约50 ms，属该设备示例，非通用指标）。

静态无功资源在额定电压下出力固定，容量随电压平方变化，按系统条件手动或自动投切，接入后提供固定的额定无功贡献。

该对比属概念层面；具体设备响应时间与投切策略取决于设备类型和运行条件。
missing_information: 给定NERC资料未给出各类静态装置的具体投切判据与电压整定值；如需具体数值需另附资料。

range within a specified voltage bandwidth in response to grid voltage changes. These resources operate 
to maintain a set point voltage or operate in a voltage droop mode. Many dynamic reactive resources, 
particularly newer ones employing power e lectronics, can respond within electrical cycles using fast -
acting controls. For example, Static Synchronous Compensators ( STATCOMs) have a response time of 
around 50 ms. 
• Static reactive resources have fixed reactive power output at their nominal voltage, and their capability 
varies according to voltage squared.  These devices are switched in or out of service based on system 
conditions. Switching action can be manual or automatic , but this type of  resource provides a fixed 
nominal contribution of reactive power to the grid once connected.

initial_answer.text:
按NERC《无功规划》指南，动态无功资源随电网电压变化在指定电压带宽内连续、实时自动调节出力，可维持设定电压或按电压下垂特性运行；采用电力电子装置的设备调节可在电气周波级完成（如STATCOM响应约50 ms，属该设备示例，非通用指标）。

静态无功资源在额定电压下出力固定，容量随电压平方变化，按系统条件手动或自动投切，接入后提供固定的额定无功贡献。

该对比属概念层面；具体设备响应时间与投切策略取决于设备类型和运行条件。

initial_answer.text:
按该NERC准则，输配（TO-DP）边界通常用有功与无功明负荷表示，可置于变电站高压侧，也可置于降压变压器及等效配电阻抗之后。

边界所建负荷功率因数（LPF）会影响大电力系统的电压与无功表现，故TO与DP须协调确定峰、轻载等临界负荷水平处的LPF。

双向要求：负荷不应过度依赖BES的滞后或超前无功支撑，BES也不应单独依赖负荷提供无功支撑。
assumptions: 仅依据所给的NERC《Reactive Power Planning》准则第37页文字作答。
该准则为北美大电力系统的自愿性建议，非中国强制标准。

Reactive Power Coordination 
 
Reactive power and voltage control should be coordinated across operating entities. Key points for coordination 
between the generation, transmission, and distribution system, as well as between entities on these systems is 
described in this section. 
 
Transmission to Distribution Coordination 
 
Modeling 
The boundary between TO and DP in power flow , stability analysis, and real-time is usually defined by explicit 
loads modeled as MW and Mvar. These loads may simply be modeled on the high side of the bus/substation or 
potentially modeled behind the step-down transformers and/or equivalent distribution impedances. The voltage 
and reactive power performance of the BES can be impacted by the load power factor (LPF) modeled across the 
TO-DP boundary. Loads should not over-rely on reactive support (lagging or leading) from the BES . Conversely, 
the BES should not solely depend on the load for reactive support (lagging or leading). Coordination between the 
TO and DP is important in determining what the proposed LPF should be at critical load levels (e.g., peak and light 
load).

This covers all clauses of the answer, including the 'usually' hedge and both alternative placements. Reactive power and voltage control should be coordinated across operating entities. Key points for coordination 
between the generation, transmission, and distribution system, as well as between entities on these systems is 
described in this section. 
 
Transmission to Distribution Coordination 
 
Modeling 
The boundary between TO and DP in power flow , stability analysis, and real-time is usually defined by explicit 
loads modeled as MW and Mvar. These loads may simply be modeled on the high side of the bus/substation or 
potentially modeled behind the step-down transformers and/or equivalent distribution impedances. The voltage 
and reactive power performance of the BES can be impacted by the load power factor (LPF) modeled across the 
TO-DP boundary. Loads should not over-rely on reactive support (lagging or leading) from the BES . Conversely, 
the BES should not solely depend on the load for reactive support (lagging or leading). Coordination between the 
TO and DP is important in determining what the proposed LPF should be at critical load levels (e.g., peak and light 
load).

initial_answer.text:
按NERC《无功规划》指南：N-1指失去单个元件后，系统在无操作员干预下仍应处于应急热额定值与电压限值内，并同时适用于稳态与稳定要求。

N-2仅涉及“选定”的部分双重故障，用于确定稳定极限，且应能承受极端扰动而不发生电压崩溃、连锁或失稳。

“无操作员干预”在段落中明确绑定的是N-1（单一故障）后的即时性能要求，而非N-2或正常工况。
assumptions: 依据为NERC2016年《Reliability Guideline: Reactive Power Planning》第21页，属自愿性指南，非中国运行标准。

excerpts.text:
Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

review.rationale: The excerpt states contingency analysis ensures the system stays within emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after loss of an element (single contingency or N-1) without operator intervention, and that this N-1 condition applies to both steady state and stability requirements. Every clause of the target (loss of a single element, no operator intervention, emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits, applicability to both steady state and stability) is directly established. Attribution to the NERC reactive power planning guideline also matches the source metadata. Contingency Analysis 
The BPS is planned and operated within its equipment normal thermal ratings and system voltage limits for 
conditions where all scheduled elements are in service (Normal condition). Contingency analysis is conducted to 
ensure that the system stays within its emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after a 
disturbance involving the loss of an element (single contingency or “N-1” condition), but without operator 
intervention. The system should be capable of such performance at all times ,26 including operations during 
minimum and maximum forecasted load conditions. This “N-1” condition applies to both steady state and stability 
requirements. In addition to satisfactory performance for normal system conditions and for single contingencies, 
the system should be able to withstand some selected “N-2” contingencies when determining stability limitations 
and also extreme (more severe but less probable) disturbances without suffering voltage collapse, cascading, or 
instability.

review.rationale: The source states that contingency analysis ensures the system stays within emergency thermal ratings and voltage limits immediately after loss of an element (single contingency, N-1) but without operator intervention, and that this N-1 condition applies to both steady state and stability requirements. All clauses of the proposition — single-element loss, no operator intervention, emergency thermal and voltage limits, and applicability to both steady state and stability — are present. The proposition is a restatement of this content and does not claim an instance application.
